source_questions.stem: A service lift is descending but its downward speed is decreasing. Taking upward as positive, what direction must its net force point?

options.A: Upward, since its acceleration opposes its downward velocity.
options.B: Downward, because it is moving downward.
options.C: Zero, because the slowing is steady.
options.D: The direction cannot be inferred without its mass.

qrt_contract.protected_work_W: Deceleration while descending is upward acceleration, not upward velocity.

rival_demands.rejection_rationale: Requires dynamic physical reasoning, not isolated recall.

factor_evidence.system_coupling: Score 1: Only the lift cabin's motion is evaluated.
factor_evidence.vector_dimensionality: Score 2: Up is chosen positive although velocity is downward.
factor_evidence.constraint_latency: Score 1: Mass and slowing trend are supplied directly.
factor_evidence.domain_coupling: Score 2: Translate change of velocity into acceleration then use Newton II.
factor_evidence.math_friction: Score 1: Only a sign inference, no equation system.

A.diagnostic: Since the downward velocity becomes less negative, a_y is positive and so is ΣF_y.

B.diagnostic: Incorrect: Velocity direction and acceleration direction need not agree.

C.diagnostic: Confuses the named system or the governing invariant; Deceleration while descending is upward acceleration, not upward velocity.

D.diagnostic: Fails the declared force/momentum direction or a dimensional check; At constant downward velocity a_y becomes zero.

source_questions.stem: Two small robots pull against the ends of the same taut strap. Robot A pulls the strap left with 40 N. Which two forces make a Newton-third-law pair at A's connection to the strap?

options.A: A's leftward pull on the strap and the strap's 40 N rightward pull on A.
options.B: A's pull on the strap and B's pull on the strap.
options.C: A's pull on the strap and A's weight.
options.D: The strap's force on A and the floor's force on A.

qrt_contract.protected_work_W: Newton-third-law partners act on different owners at the same interaction.

rival_demands.rejection_rationale: Requires dynamic physical reasoning, not isolated recall.

factor_evidence.system_coupling: Score 3: Two tugging robots form one force-interaction pair.
factor_evidence.vector_dimensionality: Score 2: Opposite horizontal arrows need owner labels.
factor_evidence.constraint_latency: Score 1: The interaction is explicitly specified.
factor_evidence.domain_coupling: Score 1: One third-law principle is sufficient.
factor_evidence.math_friction: Score 1: No algebra beyond equality of magnitudes.

A.diagnostic: A exerts 40 N on the strap to the left; that same connection exerts 40 N on A to the right.

B.diagnostic: Incorrect: A pair cannot be two forces drawn on one single-body FBD.

C.diagnostic: Confuses the named system or the governing invariant; Newton-third-law partners act on different owners at the same interaction.

D.diagnostic: Fails the declared force/momentum direction or a dimensional check; The two forces have identical magnitude even if robot A accelerates.
